snp3.10:0.2:
SN 6:10 contains a shorter, less graphic version of this sutta.

See also: MN 45; MN 97; MN 130; MN 135; MN 136; SN 35:135; SN 42:8; AN 3:101; AN 4:111; AN 5:129; AN 8:7–8; AN 8:40; Dhp 306–319; Iti 18; Iti 20; Iti 30; Iti 32; Iti 64; Iti 70; Iti 81
snp3.10:1.3: Kokālika is a bhikkhu, or Buddhist monk. Normally, the texts refer to Buddhist monks as Ven. So-and-so, but in this case, the following story will show why posterity did not accord this honor to Kokālika. According to SnA, this Kokālika was not the same Kokālika who was one of Devadatta’s followers. If that is so, it’s remarkable that both Kokālikas expressed mistrust of Ven. Sāriputta and Moggallāna in exactly the same words (see Cv VII.4.2). An alternative possibility is that the two Kokālikas were actually the same person, and that he participated in Devadatta’s schism during the “not long” period mentioned in this sutta separating his denunciation of Sāriputta and Moggallāna from the onset of his resulting disease.
snp3.10:3.3: This is an exaggerated form of address. See Ud 8:7, note 1.
snp3.10:8.1: Reading vassa-satassa vassa-satassa with the Burmese edition. The Sri Lankan version reads, “every hundred years, every thousand years.” The Thai edition reads, “every hundred years, every thousand years, every hundred thousand years.”
snp3.10:8.11: Perhaps it goes without saying that the names of some of worst hells are ironic. SnA asserts that these are not separate hells, but simply different periods of time in the single Avīci hell, but it gives no explanation or justification for its assertion.
snp3.10:10.3: The word for wickedness, kali, is the same as the word for a bad throw at dice, which becomes the image in the following verse.
snp3.10:12.4: The version of this sutta at SN 6:10 ends here.
snp3.10:13.4: This verse = Dhp 306 and is also found in Iti 48.
snp3.10:26.1: Vettaraṇin: Literally, “having a battle of twigs/canes.” SnA identifies this as the river of lye-water mentioned in MN 130, which contains a similarly graphic description of hell.
snp3.10:28.2: Reading passati with the Thai and Sri Lankan editions. The Burmese edition has phusati, “touch.”
snp3.10:29.3: A crore is a large number that SNA calculates as equal to ten million.
